text:
alex: Heads-up — hit a weird edge with the Python SDK stream API when the server sends SSE/chunked responses. Final chunk sometimes never arrives and the async generator never finishes, so cancellation hangs.

alex: Minimal repro I used (async):
```py
async with RedwoodClient(api_key=token) as c:
    async for chunk in c.stream_generate(model="small-rl"):
        if chunk.strip() == "[END]":
            break
# sometimes never gets here even though server closed the socket
```

alex: Environment: py 3.11, sdk 0.9.3, aiohttp 3.9.2, kubernetes ingress (nginx) in front.

jamie: Which transport? aiohttp vs httpx? any retries/proxies?

alex: aiohttp transport. No custom retry policy. Repro is intermittent but pretty common under moderate load (bursty).

sophia: This sounds like the old backpressure/terminator detection bug — our SSE parser currently treats an empty payload or a single-newline chunk as "no data" and keeps waiting for a non-empty data frame. If the server writes a final "\n" and closes, the reader may not yield a final event.

carla: Oof. Do we expose a way to cancel the underlying request from the generator? async generators should support .aclose() — does our wrapper forward that?

alex: I tried `await agen.aclose()` but it hangs if the transport read is blocked. Also `task.cancel()` on the outer task leaves resources stuck in event loop.

sophia: If the transport read call is blocked inside `await reader.readany()` then cancelling the generator might not interrupt it depending on where the await boundary is. Two quick ideas: add a read timeout on the low-level socket or detect EOF on connection close and synthesize a final event.

jamie: Can you paste the small raw log around the time? any exception trace?

alex: Log snippet:
```
INFO  2026-02-18T14:12:07.123Z connection=abcd read=awaiting_chunk
DEBUG 2026-02-18T14:12:07.456Z recv: b'\ndata: {"text":"..."}\n\n'
DEBUG 2026-02-18T14:12:07.457Z server closed connection (FIN)
DEBUG 2026-02-18T14:12:07.457Z client awaiting next data chunk (blocked)
```

alex: So server sent a data frame and then a final blank line / FIN. The SDK didn't produce the final `DONE` style message I expect and the generator stayed open.

sophia: Repro notes: our SSE parser checks for lines starting with `data:` and collects until an empty line. But if the final flush is only `\n` and the socket closes right after, the parser's loop sometimes never hits the newline branch because it was waiting on `read()` that returned b'' (EOF) and we didn't treat EOF as end-of-event. Will open a PR to treat EOF as if an empty line was received.

carla: Beyond the bugfix, we should add a public `Stream` object that exposes `cancel()`/`close()` for both sync and async clients so users aren't forced to rely on generator semantics. Also document `aclose()` behavior.

jamie: Filing an infra ticket and linking test flake: INF-4123 created (https://tracker/redwood/INF-4123) — assigning to @sophia and @eng-runtime to review.

deploy-bot: CI: test_stream_cancel flaky on linux-aio (FAILED) — retry queued by CI (build/12844).

alex: I can try the EOF-as-empty-line patch locally. Quick workaround for users: wrap the async iteration in a timeout: `asyncio.wait_for(agen.__anext__(), timeout=5)` and then `await agen.aclose()` in finally. Ugly but workable.

sophia: Agree on workaround. I'll add unit tests that simulate: 1) final chunk is `\n` then FIN, 2) final chunk is zero-length read (EOF) with no trailing newline. Also will add a small note in the Python SDK changelog about `aclose()` semantics.

alex: Thanks — will validate a patch when you post it. :thumbsup:

carla: Filed meta proposal to add `Stream` API for v1.0 (RDW-STREAMS-5). We'll discuss on Monday.

jamie: cc @devex for docs update once PR lands.

alex: Awesome — keeping this thread for follow-ups.
